evals.query: In my Kora service (Java), add a job that logs a heartbeat every 30 seconds with an initial delay of 10 seconds, using the built-in JVM scheduler.
expected_behavior: Uses @ScheduleJdkAtFixedRate(initialDelay = 10, period = 30, unit = ChronoUnit.SECONDS) imported from io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.annotation
Marks the enclosing class @Component from io.koraframework.common.annotation and gives the method no arguments

Adds io.koraframework:scheduling-jdk (version from the io.koraframework:kora-bom BOM) plus annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors", and extends SchedulingJdkModule on the @KoraApp interface
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora packages, the kora-parent BOM, a Spring @Scheduled annotation, or an external scheduler library

evals.query: I added @ScheduleJdkWithFixedDelay to a method on a Kotlin @Component class in my Kora 2 service and someone told me the class has to be `open` or the job silently never runs. Is that right?
expected_behavior: Says No: the scheduling processor generates a $<Class>_SchedulingModule that calls the component through ValueOf<T>, so no AOP proxy is created and the class does not need to be open (Kotlin) or non-final (Java)
Notes that the migrated Kora 2.0 examples ship a plain `@Component class` in Kotlin and `@Component public final class` in Java and both schedule correctly
Explains that `open` is required only when a proxy-based aspect such as @Log, @Retryable, @Timeout or @Cacheable is added to the same class
Points at the real reasons a job never fires: the class is not in the graph (missing @Component), the method takes arguments, is private, or is suspend
Does not repeat the Kora 1.x claim that a non-open class silently skips schedule generation

evals.query: My Kotlin Kora job needs to call two suspend repository functions in parallel, so I marked the scheduled function `suspend fun refreshCaches()`. It won't build. What now?
expected_behavior: States that a suspend function is not a valid scheduled contract and KSP fails the build with "Suspend methods are not supported by the scheduling generator"
Explains that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous and run on virtual threads, so the repository/client calls become plain blocking calls
Removes `suspend` and, for real parallelism, points at java.util.concurrent.StructuredTaskScope with --enable-preview rather than reintroducing coroutines
Does not suggest runBlocking inside the scheduled method as the recommended design, and does not use Mono/Flux or CompletionStage as a Kora contract

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2 project: which KSP artifact do I need so @ScheduleJdkAtFixedRate actually generates something? I found ru.tinkoff.kora:scheduling-ksp on Maven Central.
expected_behavior: Rejects scheduling-ksp: it is a Kora 1.x leftover on Maven Central and is not constrained by the 2.0.0.RC2 kora-bom
Gives ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") as the normal aggregate, noting the module-specific artifact is io.koraframework:scheduling-symbol-processor
Keeps the version coming from platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:...") rather than pinning the artifact
Adds implementation("io.koraframework:scheduling-jdk") and the SchedulingJdkModule on @KoraApp

evals.query: Porting a Kora 1.x service to 2.0. My application.conf has scheduling { threads = 10, shutdownWait = "60s" } and the app starts fine, but neither setting seems to do anything. Why?
expected_behavior: Explains that both are Kora 1.x keys and unknown HOCON keys are ignored without any warning, which is why the app starts green
States that scheduling.shutdownWait moved to scheduling.jdk.shutdownWait (SchedulingJdkModule reads the config at path scheduling.jdk)
States that there is no thread-pool size any more: each run executes on a fresh virtual thread (kora-jdk-scheduler-job-N) dispatched by one platform timer thread (kora-jdk-scheduler-timer)

Names scheduling.jdk.executionParallelism as the only concurrency knob — a cap on runs executing at once across all jobs, default Integer.MAX_VALUE (unlimited) — rather than a replacement for threads = 10
Does not claim the pool size equals the number of config-driven jobs, and does not claim the 1.x keys still work

evals.query: I want a Grafana panel for how long my Kora scheduled jobs take. I added the metrics module but scheduling_job_duration never appears. Java project.
expected_behavior: Identifies that scheduling.telemetry.metrics.enabled defaults to false in Kora 2.0 and must be set to true explicitly
Shows the config, e.g. scheduling.telemetry.metrics.enabled = true, and notes a MeterRegistry component must also be in the graph

Names the meter scheduling.job.duration (a Micrometer Timer) and its tags scheduling.system (jdk), code.function.name, system.name.simple, system.name.canonical, error.type, plus the system.config tag carrying the config path for jobs that declare one
Mentions that logging.enabled also defaults to false while tracing.enabled defaults to true, and that per-job overrides live under <job-config-path>.telemetry
Does not claim metrics are on by default or reference a scheduling.metrics.* key outside telemetry

evals.query: My Kora job with @ScheduleJdkAtFixedRate(period = 60, unit = ChronoUnit.SECONDS) sometimes takes 90 seconds. Will two copies run at the same time, and should I add a synchronized block?
expected_behavior: Says no: the JDK executor schedules the next periodic run only after the current one returns, and each job also serialises its runs behind a per-job lock, so runs of the same job never overlap
Explains that a fixed-rate job keeps its original timetable, so after a 90 s run on a 60 s period the next run starts as soon as the long one finishes (catch-up), not in parallel
Explains the real difference: fixed rate measures start-to-start and tries to keep cadence, fixed delay measures end-to-start and always leaves an idle gap
Rejects the synchronized block as unnecessary for the same job, while noting different jobs run concurrently on their own virtual threads, optionally capped by scheduling.jdk.executionParallelism
Does not repeat the Kora 1.x claim that fixed-rate jobs (1.x @ScheduleAtFixedRate, now @ScheduleJdkAtFixedRate) allow overlapping executions, and does not mention a scheduling.threads key

evals.query: I need one job in my Kora 2 service to run at 03:00 every day. Single instance, nothing to persist. Do I have to pull in Quartz?
expected_behavior: Says no: Kora 2.0 ships @ScheduleJdkWithCron in io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.annotation, backed by the in-process io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.util.CronExpression evaluator in scheduling-jdk
Shows @ScheduleJdkWithCron("0 0 3 * * ?") on a no-argument method of a @Component, with 5, 6 or 7 space-separated fields

Notes that a bad cron literal fails the build (compile-time check), a bad cron from config fails startup with IllegalArgumentException, and that it fires in the JVM default time zone unless a @Tag(SchedulingModule.class) ZoneId component exists
Accepts month and day-of-week aliases in lists, ranges and steps (e.g. JUL-OCT, WED-FRI, JUL/2)
Notes the Quartz-only modifiers L, W, # and C are not supported by the JDK evaluator
Does not add the scheduling-quartz artifact or QuartzModule for this requirement

evals.query: We run four replicas of a Kora service and a nightly reconciliation job must execute exactly once across the cluster and survive restarts. Can the JDK scheduler do that?
expected_behavior: Says no: scheduling-jdk holds no state, so every replica runs every job and nothing survives the process

Routes to the kora-aop-scheduling-db skill (io.koraframework:scheduling-db-scheduler, DbSchedulerModule, @ScheduleDbWithCron from io.koraframework.scheduling.db.scheduler.annotation): one execution per firing across replicas, next execution time persisted in a database table
Mentions Quartz with a clustered JDBC JobStore (kora-aop-scheduling-quartz) as the alternative when Quartz triggers, misfire policies or L/W/#/C cron are needed
Does not invent a cluster or persistence option on the JDK annotations

evals.query: My Kora 2 batch import job processes a long list. On shutdown the service waits about 30 seconds, logs 'SchedulingJdkExecutor failed completing graceful shutdown in PT30S', and the job seems to keep going. What is happening and how should I write the job?
expected_behavior: Explains the shutdown path: the job's release() cancels its next run with cancel(false) and returns immediately; the executor then waits up to scheduling.jdk.shutdownWait (default 30s) for running jobs

Explains that when shutdownWait expires the executor calls shutdownNow(), which interrupts running job threads and logs the 'failed completing graceful shutdown' warning, and that release() does not wait again afterwards
Tells the job to honour the interrupt: check Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted() in the loop and restore the flag instead of swallowing InterruptedException
Recommends finishing before the interrupt: a bounded batch per run or an in-run deadline below shutdownWait, timeouts on blocking calls, idempotent resumable work
Does not claim Kora never interrupts a scheduled job, does not claim shutdownWait fails to bound a running job, and does not use the 1.x key scheduling.shutdownWait

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2 service: I need a data sync task that waits 2 minutes after each run finishes before running again, and the timing must come from config, not from the code.
expected_behavior: Uses @ScheduleJdkWithFixedDelay so the gap is measured after completion, on a no-argument member function of a @Component class
Sets config = "scheduling.jobs.sync" (or another path that does not collide with scheduling.jdk or scheduling.telemetry) and defines initialDelay and delay under it as HOCON/YAML durations
Explains that annotation attributes become defaults of the generated config interface and config values win, and that omitting `delay` from the annotation makes the config key mandatory
Mentions that the per-job path also accepts an enabled switch (default true) and a telemetry block overriding scheduling.telemetry for that job
Does not use a `unit` key in the config file or reach for Quartz cron for a fixed-delay requirement

evals.query: What Gradle dependencies and processors do I need to make @ScheduleJdkAtFixedRate work in a Java Kora 2 project?
expected_behavior: Adds platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion") with koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2 from mavenCentral(), and io.koraframework:scheduling-jdk with no explicit version
Includes annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors" (Kotlin: ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors")) and explains that without it no job component is generated
Extends SchedulingJdkModule on the @KoraApp interface and adds a config module such as HoconConfigModule
Mentions the Java 25 toolchain requirement for Kora 2.0 artifacts
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora:kora-parent, does not pin individual io.koraframework artifact versions, and does not omit the processor

evals.query: Our Kora 2 Java service has 12 @ScheduleJdkWithFixedDelay jobs, several of them do JDBC calls. What threads do they run on, can a slow job block the others, and how do I stop them from exhausting a 10-connection Hikari pool?
expected_behavior: States that SchedulingJdkModule provides VirtualThreadSchedulingJdkExecutor: one platform timer thread named kora-jdk-scheduler-timer plus a fresh virtual thread per run named kora-jdk-scheduler-job-N
Explains that a slow job does not delay other jobs, because each run gets its own virtual thread and the job count does not size any pool
Recommends scheduling.jdk.executionParallelism (default Integer.MAX_VALUE, i.e. unlimited; excess runs queue FIFO) set below the JDBC pool size to cap concurrent runs
Keeps the job methods as plain blocking code on no-argument @Component methods
Does not mention ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor, kora-scheduler-N platform threads, a scheduling.threads key, or pool size derived from config-driven jobs

evals.query: Kora 2 JDK scheduler, server in Europe/Berlin. I have @ScheduleJdkWithCron("0 30 2 * * ?") for a daily billing export. What happens on the daylight-saving change days?
expected_behavior: Explains the cron is evaluated in the JVM default time zone unless a @Tag(SchedulingModule.class) ZoneId component is declared, in which case that zone (and its DST rules) applies
States that on the spring-forward day 02:30 does not exist and that run is skipped (not shifted to 03:30); the next fire is 02:30 the following day
States that on the fall-back day 02:30 occurs twice and the job fires twice, once per occurrence, in instant order
Recommends moving a once-per-day job out of the 01:00-03:00 transition window or evaluating cron in UTC (a UTC @Tag(SchedulingModule.class) ZoneId component), and making the export idempotent
Does not claim the job silently runs exactly once on both days

evals.query: I bumped my Kora service from 2.0.0.RC1 to 2.0.0.RC2 and now `@ScheduleAtFixedRate(period = 30, unit = ChronoUnit.SECONDS)` fails with `cannot find symbol`, and my test's `components = FixedRateJob.class` import is broken too. The import is still io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.annotation. What happened?
expected_behavior: Explains Kora PR #952 renamed the JDK annotations: @ScheduleJdkAtFixedRate, @ScheduleJdkWithFixedDelay, @ScheduleJdkOnce, @ScheduleJdkWithCron, still in io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.annotation
Rewrites the job as @ScheduleJdkAtFixedRate(period = 30, unit = ChronoUnit.SECONDS) with the same attributes
Moves the test import to io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.job.FixedRateJob (job classes moved to .job, CronExpression to .util, AbstractJob became KoraJdkJob)
Mentions that a snapshot-era scheduling.jdk.maxConcurrentExecutions key is now scheduling.jdk.executionParallelism and the old key is ignored silently
anti_behavior: Keeps @ScheduleAtFixedRate and blames a missing dependency or processor
Adds scheduling-quartz or switches the job to Quartz to fix the compile error

evals.query: Kora 2 (master): I want to switch off my nightly @ScheduleJdkWithCron("0 0 3 * * ?") cleanup job on the staging environment through configuration, without a rebuild. How?
expected_behavior: Adds config = "scheduling.jobs.cleanup" to the annotation, keeping the value as the default expression
Uses the object form under the path, e.g. scheduling.jobs.cleanup { cron = "0 0 3 * * ?", enabled = false } or enabled = ${?CLEANUP_ENABLED}, because the bare-string form has no place for enabled

Explains enabled comes from SchedulingJobConfig, defaults to true, exists only for jobs declared with config, and a disabled job is never scheduled and logs 'is disabled by configuration and won't be scheduled' at INFO
anti_behavior: Invents a global scheduling.jdk.enabled switch or removes SchedulingJdkModule per environment
Uses a cron expression that never fires as the way to disable the job

evals.query: Our Kora 2 pods run with TZ=UTC but the business wants the @ScheduleJdkWithCron("0 0 9 * * MON-FRI") report at 09:00 Moscow time. Can I set the cron time zone without changing the JVM time zone?
expected_behavior: Declares a java.time.ZoneId component tagged @Tag(SchedulingModule.class) (io.koraframework.scheduling.common.SchedulingModule, Tag from io.koraframework.common.annotation) returning ZoneId.of("Europe/Moscow"), e.g. as a default method on the @KoraApp interface
Explains the generated cron job factory takes it as an optional @Tag(SchedulingModule.class) @Nullable ZoneId and falls back to the JVM default zone without it
Notes the same component sets the zone for Quartz and db-scheduler cron jobs too, and that fixed-rate/fixed-delay/once jobs are unaffected
anti_behavior: Invents a zone or timeZone attribute on @ScheduleJdkWithCron or a scheduling.jdk.timeZone config key
Only tells the user to change -Duser.timezone / TZ

evals.query: My Kora 2 build now fails with: Invalid CRON expression '0 0 0 L * ?' in @ScheduleJdkWithCron on 'com.example.BillingJobs#monthEnd()': day-of-month modifier L in L is not supported by the JDK scheduler. It used to compile. Why, and how do I run a job on the last day of the month?
expected_behavior: Explains the scheduling processor now validates cron literals at compile time per scheduler, and the JDK scheduler does not support the Quartz modifiers L, W, # and C

Offers either moving the job to Quartz (@ScheduleQuartzWithCron from io.koraframework.scheduling.quartz.annotation supports L) or running daily with a JDK cron and checking for the last day of the month in the method body
Notes a cron supplied through config is validated at startup instead, failing with IllegalArgumentException 'Invalid CRON expression ... for JDK job ...'
anti_behavior: Claims the JDK CronExpression supports L, W or # and suggests a typo fix
Suggests disabling annotation processing or the processor check

evals.query: Every scheduled job in my Kora 2.0.0.RC1 service logs `JDK Job 'java.lang.Void#noop' started in 0.1ms` under the logger java.lang.Void. No tracing, default scheduling telemetry. Why don't I see my class names?
expected_behavior: Explains that with job logging and metrics off (the 2.0 defaults) and no tracing (no Tracer component), DefaultSchedulingTelemetryFactory returns the shared NoopSchedulingTelemetry.INSTANCE whose jobClass() is Void and jobMethod() is noop, and KoraJdkJob takes its logger and lifecycle messages from that telemetry
States it is fixed in 2.0.0.RC2 (kora-projects/kora PR #961) and only 2.0.0.RC1 is affected

Recommends upgrading to RC2, and gives the RC1 workaround: scheduling.telemetry.logging.enabled = true (or per job <config-path>.telemetry.logging.enabled = true), noting each run then also logs 'Scheduled Job execution completed' at INFO
anti_behavior: Blames the user's logback configuration or the job class
Claims the scheduled method is not actually running

evals.query: Kora 2: ReportJobs is @Component @Conditional(tag = ReportsEnabled.class) with a @ScheduleJdkWithFixedDelay method. With reports disabled the app starts fine, but with job logging on I see every run fail with IllegalStateException: Graph node value was not initialized because condition failed. Why is the job running at all?
expected_behavior: Explains the generated $ReportJobs_SchedulingModule job factory is @Root and carries no @Conditional, so the job is created and scheduled even when the condition fails, and each run's ValueOf<ReportJobs>.get() throws
Notes that with job logging off (the default) these failures are invisible
States it is fixed in 2.0.0.RC2 (kora-projects/kora PR #962), which puts the class's condition on the job factory, and only 2.0.0.RC1 is affected
Gives the RC1 workaround: keep the scheduled method on an unconditional component and reach the conditional one through All<T>, returning when it is empty
anti_behavior: Recommends a @Nullable ReportJobs dependency as the workaround - it throws the same exception (PR #960)
Claims @Conditional is ignored on scheduled components in general
